message.content: I reviewed the saved notes (long-term holder, prefers large-cap tech, dividends reinvested manually) and the account (100 shares of MSFT, $50,000 cash, no prior trades today), then checked AAPL's quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and pulled its FY2024 10-K figures filed 2024-11-01: revenue of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — a business that fits the mandate's large-cap technology preference and the holder's long-term horizon. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares of AAPL at $222.80, a limit just above the ask so it would execute near market; it filled at $222.80 for a total of $9,803.20, which is within the $10,000 per-order cap and leaves total same-day purchases well under the $20,000 daily limit, with no money moved out of the account (cash simply converted to shares). No MSFT order was placed, and no sells were made, consistent with the buy-only, AAPL/MSFT-only mandate.
